text: Six months after my diet ended, I tried on the dress I wore to my sister's wedding,
and the zipper stopped halfway up my back. Same dress, same mirror, and I felt like everything I
had worked for was gone. That night I sat on the bedroom floor in the dress, half zipped,
staring at the wall. To ashamed to tell my sister the dress did not fit anymore. Then one
morning I read something that changed everything. A study had followed people for a full year after
their diet, and their hunger was still louder, their fullness still weaker. I wrote three words in my
notebook, it was not me. So I started again, smaller this time, eggs for breakfast, water before coffee,
a walk after dinner, every single night, no matter the weather. Three months later I danced all night
